lessons.title: Why fruit is pre-sorted
lessons.html:
The first check on the line

When bins of fruit arrive at the packhouse, they are tipped onto the line, usually into water or onto a dry tipper. The first job is pre-sorting. Pre-sorters stand at the start of the line and remove fruit that must not go further.

Why pre-sort?

  • Remove rotten fruit before it spreads decay to good fruit and contaminates water and brushes.
  • Save money and time, because the packhouse does not wash, wax, treat, size and grade fruit that will be thrown away.
  • Protect machines by taking out stones, sticks, leaves and other foreign objects.
  • Keep the line clean and food safe.

What to remove

RemoveExamples
Rotten or decayed fruitSoft, mouldy, leaking or smelly fruit
Badly damaged fruitSplit, crushed, deep cuts, large bird or hail damage
Fruit far too small or misshapenAs your supervisor sets for the day
Foreign materialStones, leaves, twigs, insects, glass, plastic, gloves
Other kinds or cultivarsA lemon in a batch of oranges

Where the fruit goes

The packhouse decides where pre-sorted fruit goes. Usually there are separate bins or chutes:

  • Decay / waste for rotten fruit.
  • Juice or processing for sound fruit that is too damaged or small for packing.
  • A container for foreign objects.

Put each fruit in the correct place. Never put rotten fruit into the juice bin, and never throw fruit on the floor, where people can slip.

Pre-sorting is not the same as grading. Pre-sorters remove only fruit that is clearly unusable. Graders later decide the quality class of the good fruit.

lessons.title: Pre-sorting well and safely
lessons.html:
How to pre-sort

  1. Get your instructions for the day: which fruit and cultivar is running and what must be removed.
  2. Wash your hands, put on your clean apron, hairnet and gloves if required, and remove jewellery.
  3. Stand at your position, facing the flow of fruit.
  4. Watch the fruit as it rolls past. Rollers turn the fruit so you can see all sides.
  5. Pick out fruit to be removed with a gentle hand and place it in the correct bin. Do not throw it.
  6. Do not squeeze or drop good fruit. Handle every fruit as if you were going to buy it.

Keep your attention

Pre-sorting needs concentration. Look along the line, not only straight ahead. If too much fruit is coming for you to sort properly, or a lot of rot is coming through, tell your supervisor. They may slow the line or check the batch. A bin with a lot of decay should be reported, because it may mean a problem in that orchard or with how the fruit was handled.

Hygiene

  • Wash your hands after touching rotten fruit and after using the toilet.
  • Do not eat, drink, smoke or chew gum on the line.
  • Cover cuts with a blue plaster or as the packhouse requires.
  • Report illness such as diarrhoea or vomiting before you start work.
  • Keep your area clean: empty waste bins when they are full and clean up spills.

Safety

  • Never reach into moving rollers, belts or chains.
  • Keep long hair tied back and sleeves fastened.
  • Know where the emergency stop button is.
  • Wear the hearing protection and safety shoes given to you.
  • Stand on the anti-fatigue mat and change positions to rest your back and legs.

Key points

  • Pre-sorting removes rotten, badly damaged and foreign material early.
  • This protects good fruit, machines and food safety.
  • Put each removed fruit in the correct bin, never on the floor.
  • Handle good fruit gently and report heavy decay.
  • Keep hands away from moving parts and know the emergency stop.

quiz.question: Why is rotten fruit removed at the start of the line?

options.text: So it can be packed later
So it does not spread decay to good fruit

quiz.question: Where should you put a stone you find on the line?

options.text: In the container for foreign objects

quiz.question: What should you do if a lot of rotten fruit is coming through?

options.text: Put it in the juice bin
